svg.text: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean
Scenario: a secret is blocked without copying its value into the scan log
Ordinary work passes in both modes
A detected value stays out of the log

g.text: Given clean framework projects use Docker and binary scanners from their install answers
Two projects generated with different install answers. The Docker one keeps the Taskfile default, "docker". The binary
one answered that its runners refuse privileged containers, and its .env.dist says TASK_BETTERLEAKS_MODE=binary.
Each has a clean commit and a clean staged change, so no scan reads an empty input.
Then full, staged and branch scans pass on ordinary work in both modes
The three scans, in each project. All six print their own "No secrets detected" line.

text.tspan: task betterleaks:scan-full && task betterleaks:protect && task betterleaks:scan-branch

g.text: When a synthetic password is committed and staged in both projects
Only a synthetic password is used. One line is committed and a second one is staged, so every scan has a real finding to
Then full scans block the secret and redact its value in both modes
The full scan finds both lines. Each finding names the rule generic-password, the file and the line, and shows
And staged scans block the secret and redact its value in both modes
The staged scan finds the staged line, line 2, and hides its value the same way.
And branch scans block the secret and redact its value in both modes
The branch scan finds the committed line, line 1, in the commit that added it, and hides its value the same way.
